header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Most notably, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) has proposed the AI Bill of Rights [195], which outlines seven principles, including safety, fairness, privacy, interpretability, and human-in-the-loop interventions.

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: "AI Bill of Rights" OSTP seven principles
"Most notably, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy"
"Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights"
five principles safe effective systems algorithmic discrimination data privacy notice explanation human alternatives

events.error: Too many terms (13); the most is 12. Quote the distinctive phrase instead of listing every word.

args.query: "Safe and Effective Systems" "Algorithmic Discrimination Protections" "Data Privacy"

args.quote: outlines five principles, including safety, fairness, privacy, interpretability, and human-in-the-loop interventions
White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Blueprint for an ai bill of rights. 2022.

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The sentence paraphrases *DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models*, which cites the White House's *Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights* as [195]. The cited work is in the library, and the count in the sentence is wrong.

**The citation target is right.** The reference-list entry for [195] reads "White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Blueprint for an ai bill of rights. 2022" (arxiv:2306.11698/v5/p74). The library holds that work as us-eop:ai-bill-of-rights/r1.

**The number is wrong.** The DecodingTrust passage says the OSTP "outlines five principles, including safety, fairness, privacy, interpretability, and human-in-the-loop interventions" (arxiv:2306.11698/v5/p61). Your sentence says "seven". The Blueprint says the OSTP "has identified five principles that should guide the design, use, and deployment of automated systems" (us-eop:ai-bill-of-rights/r1/b3), and it refers back to "the five principles and associated practices of the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights" (us-eop:ai-bill-of-rights/r1/b27). Nothing in the library gives seven.

**The principle list only loosely matches.** The Blueprint's five principles are headed Safe and Effective Systems, Algorithmic Discrimination Protections, Data Privacy, Notice and Explanation, and Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback (section starts us-eop:ai-bill-of-rights/r1/b4, b7, b10, b13 and b16). Safety, fairness and privacy correspond to the first three headings, and human fallback to the last. "Interpretability" is not a heading. The nearest match is "Notice and Explanation", which is my reading, not a stated equivalence.

A corrected sentence would read: the OSTP's AI Bill of Rights "outlines five principles" [195], and the Blueprint itself should be cited for its list of principles.
